content:
We got a large list of templates. Need to find one that when applied to the given molecule reproduces the carbonyl-ene reaction (intramolecular). The task: return mapped_rxn and template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). The search returned many entries with reaction_id and template_hash. The template_id likely is reaction_id? Or maybe template_id is the integer identifier used to search. In results, each entry has 'reaction_id' and 'template_hash'. The template_id likely is reaction_id. We need to find the appropriate template that matches the described transformation.

Our molecule: "[CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]"

This is an alkene attached to aromatic ring and a cyclopentane with OH and CF3? Actually C15 with three Fs (CF3). The carbonyl-ene reaction would involve a carbonyl group somewhere, but the molecule currently has no carbonyl. Wait the forward reaction forms carbonyl-ene product? Actually carbonyl-ene reaction: alkene + carbonyl -> new C-C bond, forming allylic alcohol. In retrosynthesis, we break C-O bond (forming OH) and C-C double bond to carbonyl? The product is the given molecule? The description says the result of the reaction is formation of new C-C bond and new stereocenter where one substituent is hydroxyl. So the product (target) has hydroxyl and new C-C bond. So retrosynthetic step would break C-O bond (the OH) and break C-C bond formed, generating a carbonyl and an alkene.

Thus we need a template that does a carbonyl-ene retro: break C-O (alcohol) to carbonyl, break C-C bond to alkene, change C=C to C-C, C=O to C-O.

Search results include many templates; we need one that matches our molecule. Could test each template with apply_template to see if it yields precursors. But many. Let's try applying first few. Use apply_template with template_id = reaction_id? The tool apply_template expects template_id. Probably use reaction_id. Let's try first entry reaction_id 1237522.
